one curve for all five fades (a new one, «top», over the hero's title)
the hero title at 1440; 48 → 88 on the ladder
checked on every build · audit clean

blocks.label: What it looks like
blocks.note: Round 5 (main) in grey, round 6 in blue, at the size each caption names. Click a picture to open it large; arrows and Escape work.

items.title: The hero's fade (1440)
items.text: The same fade on the new curve 0.5, 0, 0.5, 1: it stays clear longer over the photo and reaches the black as slowly as it left the clear, so the hairline over the cells sits on a darker ground.

items.title: A card's buy row (catalog, 1440)
items.text: The buy row's fade on the new curve: the pack shows a little longer before the cloud closes over it.

items.title: A business card (1440)
items.text: The text band: the photo reaches further down before the black.

items.title: Navbar (1440)
items.text: Every link a cell with 14px each side of its text, the cells 8px apart: the texts now stand 36px apart (before 16).

items.title: Navbar hovered
items.text: The ground is the link's own cell: 14px beside the text, about the 13px over its capitals and 15 under its baseline; 8px of nothing to the next one. Before, two neighbours' grounds overlapped by 12px.

items.title: Navbar at 1100
items.text: The eight wider cells need 708px, so every section shows from 1120 (70em); at 1024–1119 the four short sections.

items.title: The logo hovered (home)
items.text: On the home page the logo is a button that takes the page to its top (no reload), with no ground on hover. On the other pages it links home as before.

items.title: The menu (390)
items.text: Every section a cell: lines across the whole menu, the gutter on all four sides of every text (trimmed: 18px at 390), no padding of the menu's own, no line under the last cell (the menu's own closes it).

items.title: The menu at 700
items.text: From the tab bar's step (640) up to the navbar's short links (768): two columns, filled left to right.

items.title: The menu sliding in, 160ms
items.text: It slides down from under the bar (0.6s, --ease-out) and back up when closed.

items.title: Hero at 1440
items.text: The title 88.3 84.9px, on the ladder at its largest (88). Every cell padded by the gutter on both sides: a link 47 / 94 47 / 47px left / right as you see it. QQ Digits.

items.title: Hero at 1920
items.text: 90.3 88px; framed. The frame now also comes from a 1616px screen as a page condition, for Safari zoomed out.

items.title: Hero at 1024
items.text: From L the row of three cells: the title 61.1 59.1px fills its cell; links 39 / 75 36 / 36.

items.title: Hero at 800
items.text: Below L: the title at the top of the section, no lines around it, at most two words a line; the countdown's three parts side by side over the three links.

items.title: Hero at 600
items.text: Below M: the countdown and the links in two columns, sharing three rows.

items.title: Hero on a phone (390)
items.text: The title 41.5 50.5px at the top; the dock in two columns at the photo's foot.

items.title: Hero at 320
items.text: The narrowest phone: the title 48px, three lines; the caption in two lines, the digits as wide as their cell.

items.title: The cells (1440)
items.text: Before: the title's left air came from the column (the gutter) and the links' right air was the gutter plus their padding (48 / 96). After: each cell reaches the screen's edge and owns its padding, the gutter on both sides (48 / 48).

items.title: QQ Digits (1440)
items.text: Your settings: stroke 90, slit 10, corners 0.5, side 25, colon side 50, the trace at 12%. Drawn as SVG segments; each fades on in 120ms and off in 200ms.

items.title: The note (1440)
items.text: Centred on the whole cell (before: on the two rows under the day row); the day row hides, the «i» stays where it is.

items.title: The note at 800
items.text: With the parts side by side the note lies over the digits and the caption, beside the «i»; the row keeps its height.

items.title: The note on a phone
items.text: Over the whole cell, which keeps its height (the note is laid over it).

items.title: The entrance at 0.9s (1440)
items.text: Before: the whole block rose at once (0.9s). After: the row rises over 1.4s and its cells arrive part by part: here the title's second line, the countdown's day row and digits, the first link.

items.title: The entrance at 0.9s (390)
items.text: On a phone the dock rises at the photo's foot while the title comes in line by line at the top.

items.title: The pager (1440)
items.text: The current number ringed in ink 50% (before full ink).

items.title: The pager hovered
items.text: Hovered, a number only darkens to ink; no ground behind it (before an ink 6% disc).

items.ask: For gradient easing: 0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 (see the fade tuner)
items.done: Every fade is on cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) now (colors.json fades: hero, caption, panel, card, and the new top; was «ease» 0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), still 16 stops over its whole block. Nothing was saved in the tuner, so the reach (1) and the lead-ins stay as they were.

items.ask: I want the gradient easing and its values for different objects to be reflected in the report
items.done: A new section, «Fades»: the curve, and for every place its ground, curve, stops, reach and lead-in, the block it lies over, its measured lead-in at 390 and 1440, and its 16 stops drawn. The curve is also in Motion.

items.ask: 1. The links should be in 1 group (now there are 3)
items.done: One row since round 5 (every section in one list); now its links are eight cells 8px apart.

items.ask: 2. Change the profile icon to the actual one from Figma
items.done: The site's icon is Figma's own: the «profile» component (Компоненты → icons, 628:27335), the one every navbar frame of «Главная» uses; I exported it again and its path data match the site's byte for byte. If you meant another drawing (an outline person?), which node?

items.ask: 3. The bg of the links on hover should be larger, making the padding around the element more even (the gap between the links stays the same and no movement)
items.done: The ground is the link's own 40px cell, 14px each side of its text (13 above its capitals, 15 under its baseline), so it is as far from the text on every side; nothing moves. Read together with 5: the cells are 8px apart, so the texts stand 36px apart (before 16, and two hovered neighbours' grounds overlapped by 12px).

items.ask: 4. Do not reload by logo on main, do not show bg on its hover
items.done: On the home page the logo is a button: a click takes the page to its top, without a reload; it has no hover ground. On the other pages it still links home and tints like every item of the bar.

items.ask: 5. Set the gap between the links to 8px
items.done: Between the cells, 8px. The eight cells now take 708px, so every section shows from 1120 (70em, was 64em: at 1024 they ran into the tools); 1024–1119 show the four short sections.

items.ask: 1. Lines should be at full width — that's the general rule
items.done: Every line runs the menu's whole width (they were inside the gutter).

items.ask: 2. The container should not have paddings — all paddings from the menu elements, it should be equal
items.done: The menu has none; every cell has the gutter on all four sides (16 → 48; 18 at 390), its text trimmed to the capitals and the baseline so the padding is what you see. A cell is 49px tall at 390.

items.ask: 3. The last item should not have bottom border
items.done: No cell has a line under it; the lines are above the cells after the first row, and the menu's own line closes it.

items.ask: 4. On larger screens items should be in 2 columns, going from left to right and wrapping
items.done: Two columns from the tab bar's step (640) to where the burger ends (768), filled left to right, a hairline between them. A phone keeps one column of big targets.

items.ask: 5. The menu should move in from above
items.done: It slides down from under the bar (the bar now has its own ground and stands above it), 0.6s on --ease-out, and back up on --ease-move; with «reduce motion» it simply appears.

items.ask: 1. «The hero's title is bigger at L (62 → 90px)» — why it's 90? It's not by the ladder rules. And why it's not reflected in the report's chart — it's 64 at max there
items.done: It was the cell's width ÷ 4.55 capped at its size on the 1520 column, a container unit outside the scale, so the chart (which draws the roles) showed the role, 40 → 64. Now the title has its own role, type/hero 48 → 88, both ends on the ladder (type/display stays 40 → 64 for the business and about heroes); from L the title fills its cell between those two: 61.1 59.1px at 1024, 88.3 84.9 at 1440, 90.3 88 from about 1540. The chart's Type tab now draws the title as measured beside the role.

items.ask: 2. When I zoom out in Safari the left and right border of containers (hero, 3 blocks, footer) disappears; it doesn't happen with other borders; when changing width in responsive mode it doesn't happen
items.done: Only these three frames come from a container query (the column at its 1520px); every other line does not. Zoomed out, Safari measures the column's query in its own units, so «at 1520» stops being true while the column still stands at its most. The frames now also come from a page condition, a 1616px screen (where the column is at its most at any height), which Safari zooms correctly. I could not run Safari from the cloud: please zoom out there again.

items.ask: 3. Around 1550 and lower links have some additional padding on the right. The title's cell is made from top, bottom and right padding; for some reason the left one is from a higher container. On smaller screens they have strange padding on left and right
items.done: Below the max the cells now reach over the gutters to the screen's edges, and each is padded by the gutter on both sides, so their text still starts on the column: a link's text and arrow 47 / 94 47 / 47px from its cell's edges at 1440, 39 / 75 36 / 36 at 1024, 18 / 18 at 390.

items.ask: 4. Around 1000 and lower the 3 links should be placed horizontally; the same for 3 blocks inside the clock block. The title should be aligned on top left of the section, with no borders around its container, max word count in the line becomes 2 words
items.done: Below L (about 1000): the title at the top of the section, under the navbar, no lines around it, at most two words a line (it wraps to three where two do not fit); from M to L the countdown's three parts stand side by side over the three links, in three shared columns. Over the photo the title has a fade from the navbar's black (a new place, «top»).

items.ask: 5. Then on smaller screens the clock and links block should be 2 columns
items.done: Below M (about 750) the countdown and the links are two columns sharing three rows (the day and the time beside «Каталог», the digits beside «Бизнесу», the caption beside «Контакты»). The caption takes two lines there and the digits are as wide as their cell.

items.ask: 6. Min title size — 48px. Its max top and bottom padding — 48px
items.done: 48px at least (the role's start). Its padding is the gutter on all four sides, so at most 48: 35px at 1000, 47 at 1440 × 900, 48 from about 1616; from L the title sets the cells' height, so the air above and below it is that padding.

items.ask: 7. The bottom block should move in its place slower. Each cell should appear element by element: line by line for title (use gsap), row by row for clock cell, link by link for the last col
items.done: The block rises over 1.4s (--t-intro, was 0.9s); inside it the title comes in line by line (GSAP SplitText: the lines as the browser set them at that width), the countdown row by row, the links one by one, each part 0.9s on --ease-out, the next a third of the way after it. A click, a key or a scroll ends it at once. GSAP loads only on the home page (34 KB gzipped).

items.ask: 8. The text appearing after clicking the «i» icon should be optically centered — relative to the whole cell
items.done: It takes the whole cell and is centred on it, by what you see (its text trimmed in its own box and balanced: 0px of growth and 45 / 45 above and below at 390); the day row hides, the «i» stays above it and closes it. The cell keeps its height from 390 up; on the narrowest phones and with a big browser text it grows to hold the note instead of cutting it (43px at 320). With the countdown's parts side by side (M → L) it is centred on the digits and the caption, beside the «i»: centring it on the whole row would need a third of air on each side and make the row grow.

items.ask: 9. Let's use our new font (the program, so that we can animate the segments later)
items.done: The countdown is QQ Digits drawn by the program: the build draws every segment from your settings (design/digits.json, from QQ Digits) into an SVG, the script lights them; each segment fades on in 120ms and off in 200ms, the unlit ones show as a trace at 12%. «00:00:00» stays 3em wide. Technology is gone. The .woff2 and the CSS of your snippet are not needed for the program (the SVG is in the page and works without the script); say if you want the font too.

items.ask: 1. Page numbers: let's make outline 50% for the selected one. It should not change the background on hover
items.done: The current number is ringed in ink 50% (was full ink); hovered, a number only darkens to ink, no ground behind it.

blocks.title: What this changes that you may not expect
items: The navbar shows every section only from 1120 now (was 1024): 1024–1119 get the four short sections, because the eight wider cells and their gaps no longer fit beside the logo and the tools.

Below L the title stands over the photo at the top, on a new fade from the navbar (fades.top); the photo shows between the title and the dock. On phones the title is bigger (48–50px, was 40–41.5) and the dock is a two-column block at the photo's foot.
Below M the countdown is half as wide: its digits 128px at 320 (were 200) and its caption on two lines (in the narrowest cells the caption shrinks a little, to its longer line's width).
The hero's links stand closer to the screen's edge: the arrow is a gutter from it (48 at 1440, was 96), like the title's text on the other side.
The entrance hides the hero for its first moment: the title, the countdown and the links appear from 0.45s on, the last link at about 2s; a click, a key or a scroll shows them at once.
Before the clock starts, the digits show only their trace (unlit «88:88:88»), not a dim «00:00:00».

blocks.title: Round 6's measures at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Round 5 (main) struck, round 6 after it. Layout: how the hero lays out its cells. Title: its size, lines, where its text starts. Link: a link's text and arrow from its cell's edges as you see them (an outer side is the screen's edge below the max). Digits: their drawn width; caption: its lines. Note: how much the countdown's cell grows when the note opens. Nav: the links shown · the ground's air beside a text / the gap between two grounds.
